date: last-modified

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/helpers.R")
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(sf)

firms <- load_design_firms("data/design.yml")
locations <- load_design_locations("data/design.yml")
```

## Overview

India's semiconductor story is not just about manufacturing. Long before the first fab broke ground, India had become one of the world's largest bases for chip *design*. Global semiconductor companies have operated R&D centres in India for decades, and a growing cohort of Indian fabless startups is now designing chips from scratch.

This page tracks three distinct groups:

- **Indian fabless firms** — companies headquartered in India that design their own chips (including beneficiaries of the Design Linked Incentive scheme)
- **GCC design centres** — India R&D operations of global semiconductor companies that design chips
- **EDA & IP providers** — companies that build the tools and IP blocks used by chip designers (not chip designers themselves)
- **Design services & other** — firms on the Chips-DLI portal or in earlier lists that, on current evidence, do not design chips of their own (kept so readers can see why they are excluded from the fabless count)

They have different strategic implications. Indian fabless firms build domestic IP ownership; GCCs bring design expertise, talent pipelines, and integration into global supply chains; EDA & IP providers underpin the entire design ecosystem. All matter, but differently.

As of `r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %Y")`, this tracker covers **`r sum(firms$category == "Indian Fabless")` Indian fabless firms**, **`r sum(firms$category == "GCC Design Centre")` GCC design centres**, and **`r sum(firms$category == "EDA & IP Provider")` EDA & IP providers** (plus `r sum(firms$category == "Design Services")` design-services firms listed separately) across **`r length(unique(firms$states))`** states.

## Design Centre Map

```{r map, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.height=6}
locations$colour <- sapply(locations$category, design_category_color)
india <- st_read("data/shp/datameet/india-composite.geojson", quiet = TRUE)

# CartoDB Positron via leaflet-providers now serves an "API key required"
# watermark — CARTO retired anonymous free tiles. Use their current raster
# endpoint directly with a free API key (fair-use tier), read from an env
# var (set in .Renviron locally / CARTO_API_KEY secret in CI) so the key
# never lands in a git-tracked file. This basemap includes state boundaries,
# unlike Esri.WorldGrayCanvas.
carto_key <- Sys.getenv("CARTO_API_KEY")
positron_url <- paste0(
  "https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/light_all/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?key=",
  carto_key
)
m <- leaflet(locations, width = "100%", options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 4, maxZoom = 10)) %>%
  addTiles(
    urlTemplate = positron_url,
    attribution = '&copy; <a href="https://carto.com/attributions">CARTO</a>, &copy; <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright">OpenStreetMap</a> contributors'
  ) %>%
  fitBounds(lng1 = 68, lat1 = 7, lng2 = 97, lat2 = 36) %>%
  addPolygons(
    data = india,
    color = "#620d3c",
    weight = 2,
    fillColor = "#E8EAF0",
    fillOpacity = 0.1,
    group = "Official Boundary"
  ) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat,
    radius = 8,
    color = "#ffffff",
    fillColor = ~colour,
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    stroke = TRUE,
    weight = 1.5,
    label = ~lapply(paste0("<strong>", name, "</strong><br/>", city, " | ", product_focus), htmltools::HTML),
    popup = ~paste0(
      '<div class="facility-popup">',
      '<h4>', name, '</h4>',
      '<div class="popup-row">', sapply(category, design_category_badge), '</div>',
      '<div class="popup-row"><span class="popup-label">City:</span> ', city, '</div>',
      '<div class="popup-row"><span class="popup-label">Focus:</span> ', product_focus, '</div>',
      '<div class="popup-row"><span class="popup-label">Scope:</span> ', design_scope, '</div>',
      '<div class="popup-row" style="margin-top:6px;"><a href="design-firms/', id, '.html" class="btn-detail">Full Profile →</a></div>',
      '</div>'
    ),
    clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(
      showCoverageOnHover = FALSE,
      maxClusterRadius = 40,
      disableClusteringAtZoom = 9
    )
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = sapply(c("Indian Fabless", "GCC Design Centre", "EDA & IP Provider", "Design Services"), design_category_color),
    labels = c("Indian Fabless", "GCC Design Centre", "EDA & IP Provider", "Design Services"),
    title = "Category",
    opacity = 0.8
  )

m
```

---

## Indian Fabless Firms

### Two Tiers of DLI Support

The Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme reaches far more firms than its grants do. Its **Product Design Linked Incentive (PDLI)** — financial support of up to 50% of eligible design expenditure — has gone to `r n_pdli <- sum(firms$dli_support %in% "PDLI grant"); n_pdli` firms (24 projects; [official list](https://chips-dli.gov.in/DLI/financialSupport)). Another `r n_listed <- sum(firms$category == "Indian Fabless" & firms$dli_support %in% "Listed as DLI beneficiary"); n_listed` Indian fabless firms tracked here appear on the scheme's [beneficiary list](https://chips-dli.gov.in/DLI/HomePage) without a PDLI grant. The portal does not itemise what each received, but MeitY [counts 95 startups under the DLI scheme](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/jan/doc2026118760301.pdf) among the users of the shared EDA tools at C-DAC's ChipIN centre: that design infrastructure is the scheme's other strand. The scheme's reach is wide; its money is narrow.

Some firms also hold an R&D project under MeitY's separate [Chips to Startup (C2S)](https://c2s.gov.in/list_of_proposals_selected_under_c2s.jsp) programme, run jointly with an academic institution; firm profiles note these.

Each firm gets two scores (1–5), kept separate so that a hard, unfinished bet and a simpler, shipped product are not averaged into the same number:

- **Ambition**, what the firm is attempting: the average of **Domain Difficulty** (commodity digital → custom analog/RF/GPU) and **IP Ownership** (licensed cores → fully custom architecture).
- **Progress**, what it has delivered: the average of **Design Completeness** (single block → full-chip tape-out) and **Market Readiness** (pre-silicon → volume production).

Firms not yet scored show "—".

### Ambition vs Progress

```{r ambition-progress, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# Scored Indian fabless firms only (GCCs use different dimensions)
scored <- firms %>%
  filter(category == "Indian Fabless", !is.na(ambition), !is.na(progress)) %>%
  # Short labels so ~30 names fit: drop corporate suffixes and parentheticals
  mutate(short = gsub(" \\(.*\\)| Technologies| Technology| Semiconductors| Digital Innovations| Networks| Infotech", "", name))

# Quadrant labels sit in the corners; midpoint of the 1–5 scale is 3
quads <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(1.55, 5.25, 1.55, 5.25), y = c(5.05, 5.05, 0.62, 0.62),
  hjust = c(0, 1, 0, 1), vjust = c(1, 1, 0, 0),
  label = c("Shipping simpler chips", "Delivering hard chips",
            "Early and modest", "Big bets, yet to deliver")
)

# Firms with identical scores would sit on one dot and hide each other's colour.
# Spread each such group on a small ring around the true point. On a quadrant line
# (score exactly 3, which counts as "high") the offset only points into the high side,
# so no firm appears to cross a line. Labels and tooltips still use the true scores.
r_off <- 0.07
scored <- scored %>%
  group_by(ambition, progress) %>%
  mutate(k = row_number(), n_same = n(),
         # Fan the group over a half-circle if it sits on a quadrant line, else a full circle
         on_x = ambition == 3, on_y = progress == 3,
         span = ifelse(on_x | on_y, pi, 2 * pi),
         start = case_when(on_x & on_y ~ 0, on_x ~ -pi / 2, on_y ~ 0, TRUE ~ pi / 2),
         theta = start + span * (k - 0.5) / n_same,
         dx = ifelse(n_same > 1, r_off * cos(theta), 0),
         dy = ifelse(n_same > 1, r_off * 1.2 * sin(theta), 0),
         dx = ifelse(on_x, abs(dx), dx),
         dy = ifelse(on_y, abs(dy), dy),
         x_plot = ambition + dx, y_plot = progress + dy) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(scored, aes(x = x_plot, y = y_plot)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3, xmax = 5.3, ymin = 0.6, ymax = 3, fill = "#f1a222", alpha = 0.08) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, colour = "#cfc8c3", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, colour = "#cfc8c3", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = quads, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#8C8480", size = 3.4, fontface = "italic") +
  geom_point(data = filter(scored, is.na(dli_support)), colour = "#b5aca7", size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(data = filter(scored, !is.na(dli_support)), aes(colour = dli_support), size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = short), size = 3.1, colour = "#2b2b2b", seed = 7,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.5,
                  force = 3, max.iter = 20000, segment.colour = "#9a918c") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("PDLI grant" = "#2f6b4a", "Listed as DLI beneficiary" = "#f1a222"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous("Ambition (domain difficulty + IP ownership)", limits = c(1.5, 5.3), breaks = 1:5) +
  scale_y_continuous("Progress (design completeness + market readiness)", limits = c(0.6, 5.1), breaks = 1:5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

`r n_big <- sum(scored$ambition >= 3 & scored$progress < 3); n_big` of `r nrow(scored)` scored Indian firms sit in the shaded *big bets, yet to deliver* quadrant: high ambition, low progress. India's design constraint is commercialisation, not talent or ambition. Firms with PDLI grants average a progress score of `r round(mean(scored$progress[scored$dli_support %in% "PDLI grant"]), 1)`, against `r round(mean(scored$progress[scored$dli_support %in% "Listed as DLI beneficiary"]), 1)` for firms listed without a grant.

```{r indian-table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
indian <- firms %>%
  filter(category == "Indian Fabless") %>%
  mutate(
    Name = paste0('<a href="design-firms/', id, '.html">', name, '</a>'),
    `DLI support` = sapply(dli_support, dli_support_badge),
    Focus = product_focus,
    Ambition = mapply(design_score_bar_html, ambition, "Ambition"),
    Progress = mapply(design_score_bar_html, progress, "Progress"),
    Scope = design_scope,
    Node = node_sophistication,
    `Founded` = founded,
    Locations = cities
  ) %>%
  select(Name, `DLI support`, Focus, Ambition, Progress, Scope, Node, Founded, Locations)

DT::datatable(
  indian,
  escape = FALSE,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 25,
    dom = 'ftip',
    order = list(list(0, 'asc')),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(className = 'dt-left', targets = '_all')
    )
  ),
  class = "display compact stripe"
)
```

## GCC Design Centres

GCC design centres use different dimensions. **Ambition** averages **Domain Difficulty** (same as above) and **Strategic Depth** (cost centre → India-led product decisions). **Progress** averages **Design Completeness** (verification only → full-chip tape-out from India) and **India Scale** (headcount: <500 → >10,000).

```{r gcc-table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
gcc <- firms %>%
  filter(category == "GCC Design Centre") %>%
  mutate(
    Name = paste0('<a href="design-firms/', id, '.html">', name, '</a>'),
    Parent = paste0(parent_company, " (", parent_hq, ")"),
    Focus = product_focus,
    Ambition = mapply(design_score_bar_html, ambition, "Ambition"),
    Progress = mapply(design_score_bar_html, progress, "Progress"),
    Scope = design_scope,
    Node = node_sophistication,
    `Est.` = founded,
    `Headcount` = ifelse(is.na(india_headcount), "—", paste0("~", format(india_headcount, big.mark = ","))),
    Locations = cities
  ) %>%
  select(Name, Parent, Focus, Ambition, Progress, Scope, Node, Est., Headcount, Locations)

DT::datatable(
  gcc,
  escape = FALSE,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 25,
    dom = 'ftip',
    order = list(list(7, 'desc')),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(className = 'dt-left', targets = '_all')
    )
  ),
  class = "display compact stripe"
)
```

## EDA & IP Providers

These are not chip design firms — they build the electronic design automation (EDA) tools and semiconductor IP blocks that chip designers use. **Origin** separates two tiers: India centres of global EDA companies (`r sum(firms$category == "EDA & IP Provider" & !is.na(firms$parent_company))`), which are among their largest R&D centres outside the US and train much of India's design workforce, and Indian-origin IP and EDA firms (`r sum(firms$category == "EDA & IP Provider" & is.na(firms$parent_company))`), most of them small and listed as DLI beneficiaries.

```{r eda-table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
eda <- firms %>%
  filter(category == "EDA & IP Provider") %>%
  mutate(
    Name = paste0('<a href="design-firms/', id, '.html">', name, '</a>'),
    # Tier: Indian-origin firm vs India centre of a global EDA/IP company
    Origin = ifelse(is.na(parent_company), "Indian firm", paste0("Global (", parent_company, ", ", parent_hq, ")")),
    Focus = product_focus,
    Scope = design_scope,
    Node = node_sophistication,
    `Est.` = founded,
    `Headcount` = ifelse(is.na(india_headcount), "—", paste0("~", format(india_headcount, big.mark = ","))),
    Locations = cities
  ) %>%
  select(Name, Origin, Focus, Scope, Est., Headcount, Locations)

DT::datatable(
  eda,
  escape = FALSE,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,
    dom = 'ftip',
    order = list(list(0, 'asc')),
    columnDefs = list(
      list(className = 'dt-left', targets = '_all')
    )
  ),
  class = "display compact stripe"
)
```

## Design Services & Non-Chip Firms

Most of these firms are on the Chips-DLI portal's beneficiary list, but a review of their own websites (November 2026) found no chip of their own. **Type** says why: *Integrator / systems* (products built on others' chips, or not a semiconductor business), *Design services*, *Unclear product* (may design chips; too little is public) or *Site down* (not yet classified). They are not counted as Indian fabless firms and are not scored. The monthly sweep checks each for news, such as a tape-out, that would move it into the fabless list.

```{r services-table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
services <- firms %>%
  filter(category == "Design Services") %>%
  mutate(
    Name = paste0('<a href="design-firms/', id, '.html">', name, '</a>'),
    Type = design_scope,
    Focus = product_focus,
    Locations = ifelse(cities == "", "—", cities)
  ) %>%
  select(Name, Type, Focus, Locations)

DT::datatable(services, escape = FALSE, rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 15, dom = 'ftip', order = list(list(1, 'asc'), list(0, 'asc'))),
  class = "display compact stripe")
```

## City-wise Concentration

```{r city-chart, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.height=4}
library(ggplot2)

city_counts <- locations %>%
  count(city, category) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

ggplot(city_counts, aes(x = reorder(city, n, sum), y = n, fill = category)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Indian Fabless" = "#620d3c",
    "GCC Design Centre" = "#1565C0",
    "EDA & IP Provider" = "#f1a222",
    "Design Services" = "#8C8480"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Semiconductor Design Centres by City",
    x = NULL, y = "Number of centres",
    fill = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Data Coverage & Sources

This tracker is a work in progress. We aim to cover every chip-designing firm on the DLI beneficiary list and the major GCC design centres. Firms on that list that are system integrators, EMS providers or software companies are left out. If you know of a firm or centre that should be listed, please [open a GitHub Issue](https://github.com/pranaykotas/india-semiconductor-tracker/issues/new/choose) or [submit via our form](https://forms.gle/FDESu4jRksmr7FTk7).

Primary sources: MeitY DLI scheme announcements, company websites, IESA reports, press releases.
:::
